info.title: AquaTome app telemetry
info.description:
The iOS app's anonymous usage events and the crash and performance reports iOS collects for it (MetricKit), for the owner's dashboard (/_ab/ung-dung/; apps/site/worker/telemetry). The privacy policy's "Thống kê ẩn danh từ ứng dụng" says what is sent.

Off until the site says otherwise: the app sends nothing unless its config, `/app/<lang>.json`, has `telemetry: true` (absent or false: off), and nothing while the reader has turned it off (Tài khoản → Gửi thống kê ẩn danh).

Both paths take JSON from the app alone: no Authorization header, no cookie, no Origin (a request with an Origin is a browser's, and is refused). Nothing is tied to an account, and neither path sets or reads a cookie. The Worker adds the country from the edge (`request.cf.country`); the app never sends it.

Our own copies (debug and TestFlight builds, whose User-Agent carries `AquaTomeCheck/1`, as for wanted names and shop links) are stored marked as tests and left out of the dashboard unless asked for.

Limits per address (an IPv6 /64 counts as one): 600 event batches and 60 reports an hour. Past them, 429 `rate_limited`; drop the batch rather than retry it soon.

The Worker validates strictly and stores nothing it doesn't expect. A batch whose envelope breaks this contract is refused whole (400). Inside a valid batch, an event that breaks it (an unknown `t`, a field it doesn't list, a value out of range) is dropped alone, and the answer counts it.

Each stored event and report is one point in the Analytics Engine dataset aquatome_app (binding APP_EVENTS; its columns: apps/site/worker/telemetry/shared.ts).

Errors are `{error}`. Retrying helps only after 429 or 503.

post.summary: A batch of anonymous usage events from one session
post.description: Send when there are events to send (the app chooses when: on going to the background, every few minutes, or at 100 events). Each event's `at` is milliseconds since the session started; `session` is a random UUID made anew at each launch.

202.description: Stored: `stored` events, `dropped` events that broke the contract.

400.description: Error: bad_request (not JSON, or an envelope this contract doesn't describe: nothing was stored)

403.description: Error: cross_origin (the request has an Origin: a browser's)

503.description: Error: telemetry_off (the server isn't set up for it)

post.summary: One MetricKit payload, as iOS gave it
post.description:
One request per payload: an MXMetricPayload (about one a day) or an MXDiagnosticPayload (crashes, hangs and other exceptions), its `jsonRepresentation()` as `payload`, cut down by the app to what the privacy policy names (unexpected quits, hangs, launch time, memory): `metaData` with only the build, OS and device type; the exit, hang (responsiveness), launch and memory metrics; crash and hang diagnostics with their call stacks but no `composedMessage` or other free text. Network, location, display, GPU and disk metrics never leave the phone. It is wrapped with what the app knows about itself. The app can write the wrapper around the payload's bytes without parsing them. No session.

The whole request is stored as received in a private bucket for 30 days (`diagnostics/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<kind>/<id>.json`), and the dashboard keeps a summary of it (crash and hang counts, launch time, peak memory) for 3 months.

400.description: Error: bad_request (not JSON, or a wrapper this contract doesn't describe)

403.description: Error: cross_origin (the request has an Origin: a browser's)

413.description: Error: too_large (over 1 MiB, the wrapper included)

503.description: Error: telemetry_off (the server isn't set up for it)

get.summary: The app's config and handbook index: only its telemetry switch is described here
get.description: Built with the site (apps/site/src/pages/app/[lang].json.ts). The site lead turns telemetry on by adding `telemetry: true` there.

200.description: The index, with its other fields (apps/site/src/lib/app-index.ts).

telemetry.description: true: the app may send events and reports (unless the reader turned them off). Absent or false: it sends nothing.

App.description: The app's version and build, as "1.0 (114)".

Device.description: The model identifier, as "iPhone17,3" (the same for every phone of that model; a simulator's is its own, as "arm64").

Path.description: A handbook page's path on the site, as "/vi/ca/ca-neon-vua/": no host, query or fragment.

lang.description: The handbook language the app shows.

session.description: A random UUID made anew at each launch and never reused for another launch. A batch waiting in the app's queue keeps its launch's id until it is sent.

PageView.description: A handbook page shown, the app's own drawing or the web page.

ScreenView.description: One of the app's own screens shown: "lights", "tanks", "account", "fishid"…

Scroll.description: The reader reached `depth` % of a page, once per depth and page shown: 50 and 90, the site beacon's marks (apps/site/src/layouts/Base.astro), measured as it measures them: the bottom of the screen against the page's height. The same marks let the dashboard put the app's reading beside the site's.

Time.description: The page had been on screen, with the app in front, for `seconds`: sent once at each of the site beacon's marks, 30, 60 and 180 s (apps/site/src/layouts/Base.astro), for the page shown.

ShopTap.description: A tap on a shop link on a page: `href` is the site's own link (/go/<shop>/…), never the shop's address, and `shop` is the network it names.

shop.description: shopee, lazada, tiki: the network in `href`.

Action.description: How one of the app's actions ended. `kind` says why it failed ("timeout", "refused:<code>") or, for fishid, the verdict or the site's error code.

kind.description: metric: an MXMetricPayload; diagnostic: an MXDiagnosticPayload.

payload.description: The payload's jsonRepresentation(), cut down to the subset above. Its field names and units vary between iOS versions; the Worker reads what it recognises, needs none of it, and stores the rest as it is.
